findings.finding: The independent auditor's report on the fiscal 2024 financial statements includes an explanatory paragraph expressing substantial doubt about the company's ability to continue as a going concern, citing operating losses and negative operating cash flows.
findings.quote: The report also states that we have a history of operating losses and negative cash flows from operations that raise substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.
findings.section: Item 1A. Risk Factors - going concern risk factor

findings.finding: Under Amendment No. 1 signed March 11, 2025, the lenders gave only a short waiver, until May 6, 2025, of the Going Concern Covenant and the Minimum Core Assets Covenant; an event of default occurs after that date unless the waiver is extended.
findings.numbers: waiver until May 6, 2025
findings.quote: Pursuant to Amendment No. 1, the Lenders waived, until May 6, 2025 (the "Amendment Period"), our covenant obligations to (1) provide a report and opinion of our auditor
findings.section: Item 1. Business - Recent Developments; MD&A - Amendment to Credit Agreement

findings.finding: Because of the going concern paragraph, the company would already be in breach of the Going Concern Covenant, and the Agent could exercise all remedies, if not for Amendment No. 1.
findings.quote: we would be in breach of the Going Concern Covenant and the Agent would be able to exercise all applicable remedies under the Credit Agreement but for Amendment No. 1 described above
findings.section: Item 1A. Risk Factors - time-limited waiver risk factor

findings.finding: The company cannot regain compliance with the Going Concern Covenant before its next 10-K, expected around March 2026, so until then it depends on further waivers that the lenders grant at their sole discretion.
findings.numbers: next 10-K expected March 2026
findings.quote: As a result, we are dependent on continued waivers from the Lenders to avoid an event of default related to the Going Concern Covenant, which waivers are in the Lenders' sole discretion.
findings.section: Item 1A. Risk Factors - time-limited waiver risk factor

findings.finding: The company says that if its debt were accelerated it may not have enough cash or be able to refinance or sell assets to repay it, and it may have to cease operations or file a case under the U.S. Bankruptcy Code.
findings.quote: we may be forced to terminate, significantly curtail or cease our operations or to pursue other alternatives, including, but not limited to, commencing a case under the U.S. Bankruptcy Code.
findings.section: Item 1A. Risk Factors - time-limited waiver and going concern risk factors

findings.finding: As of the filing date, the company says it complies with the Minimum Core Assets Covenant.
findings.quote: As of the date of filing of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, we are in compliance with the Minimum Core Assets Covenant.

findings.finding: As part of the amendment, the company had to put back into the lender-controlled account the $40.0 million it had withdrawn for inventory in Q3 2024, which reduces its free cash, and payment of a $4.0 million use fee was only deferred to the end of the Amendment Period.
findings.numbers: $40.0 million returned to controlled account; $4.0 million use fee deferred
findings.quote: we returned to a controlled account for the benefit of the Agent and the Lenders the $40.0 million that we elected to withdraw from such controlled account during the third quarter of 2024 for the purchase of inventory

findings.finding: The waiver was costly: a $3.6 million paid-in-kind fee (2.0% of term loans outstanding, implying about $180 million of term loans) added to principal, plus near-free warrants for 6% of the common stock, along with more frequent reporting to the Agent.

findings.finding: On March 12, 2025 the board started a formal strategic review of alternatives, including a possible sale or strategic transaction and refinancing the debt, with no assurance that any transaction will happen.
findings.quote: our board of directors has initiated a formal strategic review to evaluate a broad range of alternatives, including, but not limited to, exploring a potential sale or strategic transaction and refinancing our debt.

assessment.answer: The score of 0.648 comes from a $145.5 million net loss (-28.2% of assets), a $103.0 million operating loss, liabilities at 88% of assets against a peer median of 50%, and a current ratio of 1.32 against a peer median of 2.19. The text makes things look worse than these numbers do. The 2024 loss and cash burn were made smaller by about $88.7 million of one-time gains. The auditor's going concern paragraph would by itself put the company in breach of its Carlyle term loan, and that breach is waived only until May 6, 2025. Further waivers are at the lenders' sole discretion, and the company names a Chapter 11 filing as one possible outcome. This is real distress, not an artefact, and the risk is well above the band's 4% rate.
moved_by: The going concern opinion itself breaches the Going Concern Covenant of the senior secured term loan. The company would already be in default but for a waiver that runs only to May 6, 2025.
Until the next 10-K (about March 2026), the company cannot regain compliance and depends on waivers granted at the lenders' sole discretion.

Accelerated or prepaid debt (about $180 million principal) carries a 1.4x to 1.7x minimum guaranteed return. That implies roughly $250 million to $300 million owed (derived), against $134.3 million of cash. The loan also matures July 24, 2026.

To get the short waiver, the company paid costly concessions: it put the $40.0 million back into the lender-controlled account, paid a $3.6 million PIK fee, deferred a $4.0 million use fee, and gave lenders penny warrants for 6% of the stock. This points to a weak bargaining position and less usable cash.
Management says outright that it may have to cease operations or file a case under the U.S. Bankruptcy Code. It has also started a formal strategic review covering a sale and refinancing.
Without the one-time $75.2 million Amazon fee, operating cash burn would have been about $108 million in 2024 (derived). That is far faster than the 2.77 million a month in the computed figure.

evidence_against.point: The losses are shrinking. The net loss halved to $145.5M from $304.7M, the operating loss fell to $103.0M from $264.1M, and Q4 operating cash burn was small: about $2.7M (derived from -$33.2M for the year minus -$30.5M for nine months).
At filing, the company says it complies with the Minimum Core Assets Covenant, so the only covenant actually breached is the going concern opinion covenant.

evidence_against.point: Lenders chose to waive rather than accelerate, and they took warrants worth 6% of the equity. This suggests they want to stay involved through a sale or refinancing rather than force a filing.
Restructuring cut costs sharply. The workforce fell about 40% (about 50% including the November action) and operating expenses fell $126.4M, excluding one-time benefits.

evidence_against.point: Cash of $134.3M and a current ratio above 1 mean there is no immediate cash crunch from operations alone. The term loan does not mature until July 2026, more than 365 days away.

timeline.event: Amazon merger terminated; founder Colin Angle steps down as CEO and chairman; restructuring cutting 31% of jobs announced
Amazon pays the $94.0M termination fee: $35.0M repays the term loan, $40.0M goes to a restricted account, $18.8M pays professional fees
Gary S. Cohen appointed President and CEO
Q3: unrestricted cash $99.4M; $40.0M of restricted cash drawn for inventory; Q3 operating income $7.3M; covenants in compliance
CFO Julie Zeiler steps down; a further 105 jobs cut in November
Fiscal 2024 year end: revenue $681.8M (-23.4%), net loss $145.5M, cash $134.3M, liabilities 88% of assets
Additional 10% U.S. tariff on Chinese imports takes effect
Amendment No. 1: waiver of the going concern and core assets covenants until May 6, 2025; $40.0M returned to the controlled account; $3.6M PIK fee; 6% penny warrants; new robots launched
10-K filed with a going concern paragraph; board starts a formal strategic review (sale, refinancing)

dates_to_watch: 2025-05-06: covenant waiver ends; event of default unless extended, and the $4.0M use fee comes due
Q1 2025 10-Q (around May 2025): cash burn without one-time gains, core assets covenant level, and any mention of a further waiver
Outcome of the strategic review: sale, refinancing, or a lender-led restructuring
Around March 2026: next 10-K, the earliest point the going concern covenant can be cured
would_change_my_mind: Lenders extend the waiver through the next 10-K, or permanently amend the going concern covenant
A signed sale of the company or a refinancing that repays the Carlyle loan, including its minimum guaranteed return
A sizeable equity raise or strategic investment that covers most of the loan
Quarterly results showing positive operating cash flow without one-time items after the new product launch
Toward higher risk: the waiver not being extended, a core assets covenant breach, a missed interest payment, or the hiring of bankruptcy advisors
could_not_check: How much of the $134.3M cash is actually free after $40.0M was returned to the lender-controlled account in March 2025
The exact year-end term loan principal and the current minimum guaranteed return multiple, which set the payoff amount on acceleration
Q4 2024 results excluding one-time items and Q1 2025 trading after the product launch
The lenders' intentions on further waivers and the state of any sale or refinancing talks
The current market value of the equity and how much ATM capacity remains usable
